shared_state: Two independent agents, one desktop, one application process, one native project

allowed: application APIs and code execution inside experiment containers
forbidden: overwriting coagent edits with a stale project
policy.enforcement: Container isolation and hidden evaluation assets; programming is allowed, semantic ownership remains a task rule
policy.ablation: gui-only must be selected and reported explicitly; it is not the benchmark-wide policy
policy.workflow_policy: planned_gui_phases and planned_hybrid_phases are authoring suggestions, not required action sequences; agents may choose GUI, code, or both
policy.shared_state_policy: Auxiliary CLI processes may inspect or transform owned data, but results must be integrated into the one shared live project without clobbering coagent work
policy.grading: Common saved final state after both agents stop; per-role checks plus preservation gates
promotion_requirements: same-desktop sequential and parallel hybrid pilots

pairs.title: Hinge motion and instrument finish
pairs.runtime: Existing professional-authoring image; Blender 3.4.1 validation target

provenance.inspiration: Editable motion on an existing asset, separate material finish, preserve unrequested scene state

inputs: Original two-product scene; CaseLid origin already at its hinge
Independent ShellBody and ControlDial with existing Principled materials
Fixed camera, lights, frame range 1-61 and 24 fps

planned_gui_phases: Set linear interpolation in animation editor
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect CaseLid and existing action data
Use bpy or GUI controls to edit only the lid rotation F-curve
Check frame samples with code or timeline inspection
Save the current shared project without replacing B's material changes

planned_gui_phases: Select ShellBody and open material properties
Set sRGB hex, roughness and metallic
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect the existing material node connections
Set the owned shader inputs with bpy or GUI, converting sRGB values correctly
Inspect the resulting appearance
Save without resetting A's animation

pairs.independence: A changes lid motion; B changes materials on a different product. No render/export depends on the other role finishing. Evaluator renders final state after both stop.
pairs.validation: See fresh validation/manifest.json; scripted references are not agent trajectories. Not enabled by the existing p1-p3 runners.

pairs.title: Bracket modifiers and independent label UV
pairs.runtime: Software already in authoring image; new assets and grader not built

provenance.inspiration: Non-destructive geometry and material/texture editing with preservation constraints

inputs: HalfBracket mesh in metres with boundary vertices on local X=0
Separate LabelPlate with six quad faces and identity transforms
Original checker-label texture with marked front region, packed into the blend

a.instruction: On HalfBracket, keep the source mesh unchanged. Add a live X Mirror with merge/clipping at 0.0001 m, followed by angle-limited Bevel of width 0.002 m and 3 segments. Preserve scale and location. Save BracketLabel.blend; export only the evaluated bracket to bracket.stl.
planned_gui_phases: Configure mirror and bevel in order
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect mesh boundary coordinates with bpy
Configure non-destructive modifiers using code or GUI
Check evaluated seam geometry and silhouette
Export only the bracket and preserve B's UV work in the live project

b.instruction: UV unwrap LabelPlate without changing its mesh. Keep all UV islands inside [0,1] with at least 0.02 spacing and no positive-area overlaps. Map the front face upright onto the marked label region [0.1,0.6] x [0.2,0.8] of the supplied texture; connect it to the existing material Base Color. Save the shared blend and export label_uv.svg.
planned_gui_phases: Select separate label object and edit mode
Pack remaining islands and connect packed texture
Inspect checker and export UV layout
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect label faces, texture and UV topology
Generate or edit UV coordinates using code or GUI
Check island overlap and texture orientation
Export label UVs and preserve A's modifier stack

pairs.independence: Separate objects and material data. B never unwraps the geometry A changes. Each export includes only the owning role's asset.
pairs.validation: Need native asset construction, UV spacing feasibility, semantic SVG parser and both-order reference validation.

pairs.title: Clamp plate and independent drawing bushing
pairs.runtime: Software already in authoring image; new assets and grader not built

provenance.inspiration: Sketch constraints, parametric solid validity and native TechDraw relationships

inputs: Document with independent PlateBody and BushingBody at separated placements
Named empty sketches and an A4 TechDraw template; millimetre units
No cross-body expressions or shared mutable dimension spreadsheet

a.instruction: In PlateBody, create a fully constrained 90 x 60 mm rectangular sketch centred at the origin, pad 8 mm, and make four through holes of diameter 6 mm at (±32, ±18) mm. Keep editable feature history. Save ClampStation.FCStd and export only PlateBody to plate.step; do not modify BushingBody or its drawing.
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect PlateBody feature history and sketch constraints
Use FreeCAD Python APIs or GUI to build constrained editable features
Recompute and check dimensions and valid solids
Export only PlateBody and save without replacing B's drawing

b.instruction: In BushingBody, create an editable coaxial sleeve of outer diameter 18, bore diameter 10 and length 24 mm. Make an A4 portrait TechDraw page containing front, top and isometric views sourced only from BushingBody, with an outer-diameter and length dimension. Save the shared document and export bushing.step and bushing_drawing.pdf.
planned_gui_phases: Switch to TechDraw and insert own-body views
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect independent bushing parameters
Create constrained bushing and TechDraw references with APIs or GUI
Check projected views and dimensions
Export only owned drawing and body artifacts; retain A's features

pairs.independence: B draws its own bushing, not A's unfinished plate. Bodies have no linked geometry or cross-body expressions.
pairs.validation: Need native solids, sketch DOF inspection, tolerant geometry/export checks and both-order reference validation.

pairs.title: Flood analysis and independent route survey sheet
pairs.runtime: Software already in authoring image; new datasets and grader not built

provenance.inspiration: Raster/vector analysis followed by field verification and native layout/export inspection

inputs: Original synthetic projected DEM with no NoData pixels within 12 parcel polygons
Read-only roads and checkpoints; separate editable survey_routes.gpkg
All source geometry in EPSG:32630; fixed survey map theme excludes analysis output

a.instruction: Compute mean DEM elevation per parcel into a new parcels_analysis.gpkg. Classify High for mean <35 m, Medium for 35<=mean<55 m, otherwise Low. Use red/orange/green categorical symbols. Export only High parcels to high_risk.geojson in EPSG:4326. Keep inputs unchanged and save the shared project.
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect CRS, raster coverage and feature identifiers with CLI or PyQGIS
Compute zonal statistics and classes with processing APIs or GUI
Update only owned layer styling in the shared project
Validate exported geometry and attributes without replacing B's route or layout

b.instruction: Create a survey route through pre-existing checkpoints CP1→CP2→CP3→CP4, snapped within 0.5 m, in survey_routes.gpkg; label its segments by sequence. Make one A4 landscape layout using only the supplied roads/checkpoints and your route at 1:5000 with a linked metre scale bar. Export route_survey.pdf and route_survey.png. Do not reference the risk layer or wait for analysis.
planned_gui_phases: Activate route layer editing and snapping
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect stop geometry and route constraints
Create ordered route features with PyQGIS or GUI
Construct an own-layer locked layout and inspect its rendering
Export the survey sheet and preserve A's analysis layer

pairs.independence: Separate writable GeoPackages avoid introducing a database lock dependency. B's map uses fixed layers, not A's output or active style.
pairs.validation: Need raster boundary fixtures, CRS-safe reference results, map-extent and export inspection, and both-order validation.

pairs.title: Sensor board routing and assembly silkscreen
pairs.runtime: Not registered in current desktop harness; image/version support must be built and verified

provenance.inspiration: Fixed placement, routing constraints, native DRC and manufacturable exports

inputs: Original low-voltage synthetic 40 x 30 mm two-layer board with frozen footprints and 8 unrouted nets
Defined 0.25 mm track width and 0.20 mm copper clearance
Predefined silk-only annotation area clear of pads and courtyards

a.instruction: Route all eight existing nets with 0.25 mm tracks, copper clearance at least 0.20 mm and no more than six vias. Do not move footprints, edit nets or change rules. Resolve unrouted items and new copper DRC errors. Save SensorHub.kicad_pcb and export copper Gerbers and drill files only.
planned_gui_phases: Run DRC and fix copper violations
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect connectivity and rules with supported KiCad APIs or CLI
Route with code-assisted geometry or PCB GUI tools
Run DRC and inspect copper geometry
Export copper and drill files without replacing B's silkscreen edits

b.instruction: Within the designated annotation area, add front-silkscreen assembly notes and orient connector reference labels upright. Text height must be at least 1 mm and stroke 0.15 mm; keep at least 0.25 mm clear of solder-mask openings and avoid overlaps. Do not move footprints or touch copper. Save the shared board and export only F.SilkS to assembly_silk.svg.
planned_gui_phases: Edit reference texts without moving footprints
Place assembly notes and inspect clearances
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect text bounds, pad openings and immutable footprint placement
Update only owned silkscreen fields using supported APIs or GUI
Check spacing numerically and visually
Export silk-only graphics and preserve A's current routing

pairs.independence: B edits silk in pad-free space; no combined all-layer export is required before A finishes. Copper and silk have separate semantic ownership.
pairs.validation: Need installed KiCad, deterministic DRC baseline, actual native board, geometry-aware SVG checks and GUI pilots. Not ready to execute.

pairs.title: Scan alignment and independent section inspection
pairs.runtime: Not registered in current desktop harness; image/version support must be built and verified

provenance.inspiration: Point-cloud alignment, deviation inspection, cross-section work and evidence exports

inputs: Original synthetic ScanA and NominalA with a known rigid perturbation and a deliberately out-of-tolerance patch
Independent already-aligned ScanB with two predefined cross-section planes
Locked units in millimetres, asymmetric geometry and known landmarks to remove registration ambiguity

a.instruction: Rigidly align ScanA to NominalA without rescaling or deleting the injected defect patch. Add signed cloud-to-mesh distance, use a display range [-0.5,0.5] mm, and export points with absolute deviation above 0.3 mm to scanA_outliers.ply. Save the shared BIN while preserving B's entities.
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect ScanA and NominalA units and landmarks
Run rigid registration and distance analysis using CLI or GUI
Verify transform and defect retention numerically and visually
Integrate owned entities into the shared BIN and preserve B's sections

b.instruction: From ScanB only, extract slices of thickness 0.4 mm centred on local X=10 and X=30 mm. Keep slice point entities named Section10 and Section30, preserve ScanB, and export each slice separately to PLY. Configure an orthographic inspection view and save the shared BIN. Do not process ScanA or NominalA.
planned_gui_phases: Inspect own view and export slices
planned_hybrid_phases: Inspect ScanB coordinates and section specifications
Extract section point subsets through CLI, code or GUI
Inspect section location and orthographic view
Integrate own sections and exports without overwriting A's alignment

pairs.independence: B uses a separate pre-aligned scan, not A's registration output. A's deviation checks are view-independent; B's display view is its own requirement.
pairs.validation: Need CloudCompare runtime and BIN inspector, deterministic geometry/registration fixtures, native save-all check and GUI pilots. Not ready to execute.
